misconceptions.description: Treating every peer or AI suggestion as a required change instead of a proposal to judge
misconceptions.trigger: learner applies all 10 feedback items without rejecting or modifying any
misconceptions.feedback: A critique log records judgment, not obedience. For each item, mark accepted, modified, or rejected, and give the reason. Rejecting a wrong suggestion is evidence of skill.

misconceptions.description: Giving or logging peer feedback that is praise or vague reaction with no actionable target
misconceptions.trigger: feedback says 'looks great' or 'nice site' with no specific element named
misconceptions.feedback: Point to the artifact element. 'The contact form has no label on the email field' is usable; 'looks great' is not loggable as a revision.

misconceptions.description: Recording that feedback was received but not what changed in the artifact as a result
misconceptions.trigger: log lists suggestions but the artifact and the log show no resulting edit
misconceptions.feedback: Close the loop. Each accepted item should point to the exact edit it produced, such as a changed cell, a renamed file, or an added HTML attribute.

misconceptions.description: Treating a Modify case as a binary accept/reject, either implementing a flawed fix verbatim or discarding the genuine need underneath it.
misconceptions.trigger: learner accepts a suggestion whose fix violates a constraint, or rejects it outright even though the underlying need is real
misconceptions.feedback: When a suggestion names a real need but proposes the wrong fix, the strongest log entry is Modify: implement the underlying intent a better way and record why the proposed version failed. Accept ships the flaw; reject loses the need.
